conversations.title: DISABLED BUS PASS CAMPAIGN WIN
conversations.reply: Getting the bus pass earlier means you can head out to meet someone without racing the clock. It’s a small step that cuts one more barrier out of the way.

conversations.title: Padiham man’s inclusive rave United by the Groove returns for second year
conversations.reply: It’s great to see a rave that’s truly inclusive ,  a step‑free dance floor, chill zones, and DJs who just want people to have fun. When a venue gets it right, everyone can let loose.

conversations.title: Review: Southampton Pride 2026
conversations.reply: A Trans+ zone behind stairs is a real let‑down. When a place says it’s welcoming but the door blocks you, it’s the same problem we’ve seen time and again.

conversations.title: Stonehouse charity helps adults with learning disabilities enjoy live music
conversations.reply: The grant for Gig Buddies proves a little funding can turn a venue into a music‑friendly space. When a place gets the right support, the whole night feels a lot more welcoming.

conversations.title: Great Disabled Access Bars in London
conversations.reply: A list of bars where you can actually roll in, order a drink and stay for the whole set is a breath of fresh air. These places show what a night out should feel like.

conversations.title: ‘I want to live’: the disabled people unable to go abroad because of care funding refusal
conversations.reply: Being told you can’t use your care package to travel abroad feels like a big roadblock to meeting new people. It’s frustrating that funding still treats travel as a luxury.
